title: [Bugfix] Fix CUTLASS MoE router input weighting for FP8/FP4
body_opening:

  The prepare/finalize path already applies router weights to the MoE input before quantization when `apply_router_weight_on_input=True`. Some CUTLASS expert paths still applied the same weights again on the output side, causing double weighting.

  - Fixed CUTLASS FP4 and MXFP4 paths to skip output-side router weighting when prepare already applied the weights.
  - Fixed standard CUTLASS FP8 and W4A8-FP8 paths to skip fused unpermute weighting when prepare already applied router weights.

title: [EPLB] Optimize memory overhead in Nixl communicator

title: [Bugfix] Fix SM100 fp8_ds_mla cache scales
body_opening:
## Summary

Unify the `fp8_ds_mla` cache scale contract used by FlashMLA on SM90 and
SM100. The physical 656-byte cache entry is unchanged: 512 FP8 NoPE values,
four FP32 scale fields (one per 128 values), and a 128-byte BF16 RoPE tail.
The value stored in each FP32 scale field is now always:

```text
2 ** ceil(log2(max(amax / 448, 1e-4)))
```

Power-of-two values survive both reader conversions exactly: SM90 converts
the scale to BF16, while SM100 converts it to E8M0. Arbitrary FP32 values can
therefore make the writer quantize with a different scale than the reader
uses. The `1e-4` lower bound matches the FlashMLA UE8M0 reference margin and
maps an all-zero tile to `2^-13` after rounding.

title: [XPU] Support decode context parallelism (DCP) on Intel XPU
body_opening:
## Motivation

Enable `--dcp-size > 1` (decode context parallelism) on Intel XPU. DCP shards the KV cache by token position (`pos % dcp_size == dcp_rank`) and merges each rank's partial attention output by log-sum-exp. The collectives run over oneCCL (`xccl`) through `torch.distributed`, since there is no pynccl on XPU.

DCP buys **context length, not throughput**: per-rank `max_total_num_tokens` is unchanged, so the servable context doubles at `dcp=2`.

## Modifications

Both XPU attention backends support DCP. `triton` runs on any kernel build. `intel_xpu` is the faster one, so DCP is implemented directly in `xpu_backend.py` rather than left refused.
